# Company 041 — Autonomous Micro-SaaS Factory

**Company ID:** `company:future:041`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:041`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-041-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no SaaS creation, domain purchase, deployment, billing, marketing, customer creation or public launch.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide a reusable factory for designing, building, operating, measuring, maintaining and retiring small software businesses after each product is separately authorized.

Problem: micro-SaaS products repeat the same authentication, tenancy, billing, deployment, analytics, support, security and lifecycle work; product-specific logic is often small compared with repeated infrastructure.

Value: reduce repeated engineering while keeping each product/company isolated and independently governable.

## Product tree

SaaS Product Template Library; Product/Problem Spec Generator; Shared Auth/Tenant Template; Billing/Entitlement Template; Database/Storage Template; API/Worker Template; UI/PWA/Mobile Shell Templates; Admin/Support Console; Analytics/Telemetry Template; Feature Flags; CI/CD/Preview/Staging/Production Template; Security/Privacy Baseline; Customer Onboarding; Documentation/Knowledge Base; Support Workflow; Incident/Status Template; Backup/Recovery; Cost/Unit-Economics Monitor; Product Experiment Framework; Maintenance/Dependency Bot; Product Migration/Upgrade; Portfolio Dashboard; Sunsetting/Export/Deletion Workflow; Spinoff/Promotion to larger company architecture; API/SDK/OEM for factory components.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: project scaffolding, manifests, environment isolation, modules, schema migrations, feature flags, auth/roles, tenant isolation, subscription/usage billing seams, quotas, emails/notifications, analytics, support, docs, backups, observability, test/eval packs, security scans, deployment/canary/rollback, cost caps, customer export/delete, accessibility/localization, version/deprecation.

Customers: internal portfolio builders, founders, agencies, venture studios, product teams, developers; potentially enterprise innovation teams. Verticals are intentionally broad; the factory creates domain-specific SaaS only through separate authorized project/domain packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Factory Brain knows product archetypes, shared platform contracts, historical build/runtime failures, unit economics, security patterns and product lifecycle. It reasons about whether a candidate should use an existing template, a new module or a standalone architecture; plans builds, predicts complexity/cost, recommends scope and sunsetting. It must not create or launch products without James’s authorization.

Architecture: template/manifests, module registry, Company/Project Foundry integration, Brain Factory/domain packs, Agent Factory, deployment/billing/support/testing factories, shared packages with strict versioning, per-product repo/env/data/secret boundaries, event-driven lifecycle state machine.

## Agent tree

Product Spec Agent, Architecture Agent, Scaffold Agent, Data Model Agent, UI Agent, Integration Agent, Security Agent, QA Agent, Release Prep Agent, Cost Agent, Support/Docs Agent, Analytics Agent, Maintenance Agent, Migration Agent, Incident Agent, Sunset/Portability Agent, Portfolio Analyst.

## Deterministic services

Template registry; code generator; repo/environment manifests; schema migration framework; auth/tenant service abstractions; billing/entitlement adapters; CI/CD; test runners; feature flags; config/secrets refs; deployment registry; telemetry; backup/export/delete; dependency updater; release/version ledger; budget/cost meter.

## Workflow

Owner authorizes product/company → load approved roadmap → choose product/company/project identity → select templates/modules/Brain/Agent/domain packs → generate isolated scaffold → security/data/billing/deployment configs → build/test → controlled environment → owner/protected release approval → monitor/support/iterate → profitability/quality review → scale or sunset → export/delete/archive evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

Git hosting, deployment/hosting, DB/storage, auth, payment/billing, email/notifications, analytics, support, observability, domains/DNS, model/API providers, app stores where relevant. Factory APIs for template/manifest/build/test/release/health/cost/sunset operations.

Data moat: build templates, reusable modules, failure/recovery corpus, product/architecture decision history, cost benchmarks and automated validation—not customer data pooling.

## Monetization / distribution

Could itself become a developer/venture-studio platform via seats, products, deployments, usage, premium templates, OEM/private factory, managed product operations, revenue share only if transparent. For James’s ecosystem it is primarily an internal capability until separately commercialized.

## Security/privacy/legal

Strong company/product isolation; templates must be secure by default; secrets never copied between products; customer tenancy/data boundaries; no domains/billing/legal terms activated automatically; supply-chain/version pinning; generated code requires tests and security gates.

## Failure / edge cases

Template drift, shared-package regression across products, accidental shared tenant DB, secret reuse, wrong billing config, runaway generated scope, duplicate products, abandoned SaaS, dependency EOL, deployment provider outage, product no longer economical. Use manifests, compatibility matrix, canaries, isolated versions, cost caps, sunset workflow.

## Scale / platform / overlap

Internal factory → tens of products → multi-company platform. Strong overlap with Command Center Foundry, #29 Vertical OS Generator and #53 Release Autopilot. The company is commercialization/operation of SaaS factory capability; Command Center remains leader.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** project/company templates, module manifests, isolation, versioning, deployment/billing/support/testing factory interfaces, cost telemetry, lifecycle/sunset/portability.  
**BUILD NOW:** substantial shared Foundry/factory abstractions are likely Command Center requirements after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** tenant/billing/support/deployment factory implementations and company creation transaction.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** actual micro-SaaS products and customer-facing factory product.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large product fleet/marketplace/multi-region template platform.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: templates/spec/auth/billing/data/API/UI/admin/analytics/flags/CI/security/onboarding/docs/support/incidents/backup/cost/experiments/maintenance/migration/portfolio/sunset/spinoff/API.
2. Feature Tree: scaffolding/manifests/env/modules/migrations/auth/tenant/billing/quotas/comms/analytics/support/backup/tests/security/deploy/cost/export/accessibility.
3. Customer Tree: internal portfolio/founders/agencies/studios/product teams/developers/enterprise innovation.
4. Vertical Tree: generic factory; domain packs create separately governed vertical SaaS.
5. Brain Tree: architecture/template/scope/cost/lifecycle reasoning; no unauthorized product launch.
6. Agent Tree: spec/architecture/scaffold/data/UI/integration/security/QA/release/cost/support/analytics/maintenance/migration/incident/sunset/portfolio.
7. Service Tree: template/codegen/repo/env/schema/auth/tenant/billing/CI/tests/flags/secrets/deploy/telemetry/backup/export/dependencies/version/cost.
8. Workflow Tree: authorize→select templates→generate→build→test→release approval→operate→scale/sunset.
9. Integration Tree: Git/hosting/DB/auth/payments/comms/analytics/support/observability/DNS/providers/app stores.
10. Data Tree: templates/manifests/modules/builds/tests/releases/costs/incidents/product lifecycle evidence.
11. API Tree: template/manifest/build/test/release/health/cost/sunset.
12. Monetization Tree: seats/products/deployments/usage/templates/OEM/managed/revenue-share.
13. Distribution Tree: developer/venture-studio/agency/internal portfolio ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: scaffolding/build/tests/maintenance/monitoring/cost/sunset prep; launches protected.
15. Moat Tree: reusable modules, build/recovery corpus, compatibility/cost history.
16. Platform Tree: internal factory→commercial factory→portfolio operating platform.
17. Risk Tree: isolation failure, template debt, secret/billing mistakes, mass regression, runaway scope/cost.
18. Scale Tree: one product→dozens→100+ isolated SaaS products.
19. Spinoff Tree: product templates/CI/support factories remain shared services unless independently commercialized.
20. Command Center Dependencies: Foundry, project registry, Brain/Agent factories, deployment/billing/testing/support/resource governors.
21. Design-Now Requirements: standardized manifests/factories/isolation/lifecycle interfaces.
22. Build-Now Requirements: likely core Command Center factory seams after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: external factory customers/marketplace/pricing and actual SaaS launches.
24. Autonomous Mature State: authorized products are scaffolded/tested/maintained/monitored by the factory; James decides which businesses exist, budgets and strategic pivots.

## Saturation result

Additional branches map to shared factories already required by the master directive or vertical generator #29; no new top-level company is needed.

# Company 042 — Legacy Browser Worker Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:042`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:042`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-042-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no external browser automation or credential use.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide reliable, auditable automation for authorized web portals and legacy software that lack usable APIs.

Problem: critical workflows still require humans to navigate portals, upload/download files, copy data and recover from UI changes; ordinary browser scripts are brittle and unsafe around credentials/side effects.

Value: versioned browser workflows with visual/DOM state verification, scoped credentials, replay, checkpointing, selector recovery and human escalation.

## Product tree

Browser Worker Runtime; Workflow Recorder; Visual+DOM Action Model; Selector Recovery; Portal Adapter Registry; Credential/Session Broker; File Upload/Download Worker; Form Completion; Data Extraction; Screenshot/Evidence Capture; State Verification; Checkpoint/Resume; Workflow Replay/Simulation; Change/Drift Detection; Human-in-the-Loop Step; CAPTCHA/User-Presence Boundary; Multi-Browser/Viewport; Private Runner; Queue/Scheduler; Audit/Incident Console; API/SDK/OEM; Vertical Portal Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: target allowlists, account/project scope, session isolation, page-state hash, DOM/visual anchor, action preconditions, post-action verification, timeout/retry, idempotency, downloads hash, upload provenance, MFA/user step, browser profiles, cookies/secrets vault refs, rate limits, concurrency, screenshot redaction, network log metadata, selector confidence, rollback where feasible.

Customers: operations teams, enterprises, agencies/integrators, SaaS vendors needing legacy connectors, finance/admin teams, healthcare administrative portals, logistics, procurement, public portals, compliance/credentialing systems.

Verticals: supplier/customer portals, government/admin sites, insurance/admin portals, banking read-only/admin workflows where lawful, logistics, property, healthcare admin, ERP legacy web, credentialing, ecommerce marketplaces. High-risk financial/legal actions require strict approval.

## Brain / architecture

Brain understands page state, workflow intent and likely selector recovery; it plans navigation and diagnoses UI drift. Deterministic browser policy owns allowed domains/actions, credential scope and protected-action preconditions. Page content is untrusted and cannot override system instructions.

Architecture: sandboxed browser containers, Playwright-like driver abstraction, visual/DOM model, session broker, secrets refs, workflow/state engine, artifact store, screenshot/redaction, network policy, replay fixtures, LLM/vision only for recovery/semantic element identification under hard action constraints.

## Agent tree

Workflow Recorder Agent, Navigation Agent, Selector Recovery Agent, Form Agent, File Transfer Agent, Extraction Agent, Visual State Agent, Session/MFA Coordinator, Drift Monitor, QA/Replay Agent, Security/Prompt-Injection Agent, Incident/Recovery Agent, Adapter Builder.

## Deterministic services

Browser pool; session isolation; credential proxy; domain/URL policy; action schema; selector engine; file scanner; download/upload hash; screenshot artifact service; workflow/checkpoint engine; queue; rate/concurrency limiter; network egress control; audit; protected click/submit gate.

## Workflow

Authorize target/account/workflow → establish isolated session → validate page/origin → execute bounded step → verify post-state/artifact → checkpoint → continue → on drift, attempt safe selector recovery/simulation → escalate if ambiguous/protected → capture completion evidence → destroy/expire session.

## Integrations / API / data

Browsers, secret managers, workflow engines, file/object storage, email/MFA handoff, task queues, ticketing, source systems receiving extracted/uploaded data. APIs for worker session/workflow/step/artifact/status/replay/health.

Data moat: portal adapter library, selector-recovery history, page-state fingerprints and verified workflow traces; credentials/customer payloads remain isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Browser minutes/sessions/workflows, portal adapters, enterprise/private runners, API, managed adapter maintenance, OEM. Distribution via automation/integration/RPA ecosystems, SaaS vendors, consultants.

## Security/privacy/legal

Highest-risk area: untrusted pages, credential theft, prompt injection, malicious downloads, accidental destructive clicks. Domain/action allowlists, sandboxing, download scanning, origin validation, credential broker, no secret exposure to model, screenshot redaction, human/MFA boundaries, protected-action gate, terms/access restrictions.

## Failure / edge cases

UI redesign, popups, localization, A/B, CAPTCHA, MFA, session expiry, network lag, duplicate submit, file chooser, browser crash, anti-bot, malicious page instruction, unexpected redirect, download mismatch. Use checkpoints, idempotency, state verification, strict origin checks and manual fallback.

## Scale / overlap

Few adapters → enterprise browser-worker fleet → legacy integration infrastructure. Overlap #8 workflows, #31 forms, #64 inbox, #100 modernization. #042 specializes in no-API browser execution.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** browser-worker sandbox, hostile-content boundary, session/credential refs, action verification, artifact provenance, worker quotas.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center/Agency browser-worker contracts and prompt-injection defenses likely need direct strengthening after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** isolated browser pool, credential broker, egress policy and artifact scanner.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer portal adapters/product/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large distributed browser fleet.

# Company 043 — Cloud Cost Optimization Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:043`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:043`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-043-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no cloud changes, purchases/reservations or paid-resource activation.

## Business identity

Purpose: continuously attribute, forecast and reduce cloud/software-infrastructure cost while preserving reliability/security/performance requirements.

Problem: compute, storage, database, network, GPU and AI-model spend grows through idle resources, wrong sizes, poor scheduling and architecture drift.

Value: evidence-backed cost allocation, waste detection, optimization recommendations and policy-bounded remediation.

## Product tree

Cost Inventory/Allocation; Idle/Orphan Resource Detection; Rightsizing; Schedule/Shutdown Planner; Storage Tier/Lifecycle Optimization; Database Cost Optimizer; Network/Egress Analyzer; GPU/Accelerator Optimizer; AI Model/Inference Cost Analyzer; Reservations/Commitment Planner; Spot/Preemptible Planner; Kubernetes/Container Cost; Serverless Cost; Multi-Cloud Comparison; Budget/Forecast/Anomaly; Unit Economics; Architecture Recommendation; FinOps Chargeback; Savings Verification; Policy/Guardrails; API/OEM; Enterprise Private.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: account/project/company/tag allocation, resource type/region, utilization, SLA/latency, dependencies, reserved/spot eligibility, lifecycle, data class, egress, model tokens/requests, workload schedule, anomaly, budget, forecast, recommendation confidence, projected/verified savings, remediation risk, approval/audit.

Customers: startups/SMBs, SaaS, AI companies, enterprises, platform/SRE/FinOps teams, agencies/MSPs, data/ML teams. Verticals broad; AI/GPU, SaaS, ecommerce and data-heavy workloads need specialized packs.

## Brain / architecture

Brain reasons about workload intent/dependencies, tradeoffs and architecture alternatives; predicts capacity/cost and recommends changes. Deterministic billing/utilization math and policy own savings calculations. It cannot terminate/resize/purchase resources without approval.

Architecture: cloud billing/cost ingest, resource graph, metrics/time series, rightsizing rules, forecast/anomaly models, optimization/constraint solver, policy engine, simulation, LLM for architecture explanation only with source metrics.

## Agent tree

Cost Allocation Agent, Idle Resource Agent, Rightsizing Agent, Schedule Agent, Storage Agent, Database Agent, Network Agent, GPU/AI Cost Agent, Commitment Agent, Container Agent, Forecast/Anomaly Agent, Architecture Analyst, Savings Verification Agent, Policy/Risk Agent, Multi-Cloud Analyst.

## Deterministic services

Billing/usage connectors; resource inventory/graph; metric collectors; cost calculator; budget/forecast; anomaly; rightsizing rules; simulation; recommendation ledger; savings verification; policy/approval; protected cloud-action gate; audit.

## Workflow

Ingest bills/resources/metrics → allocate/tag → detect waste/anomaly → model dependencies/SLA → simulate recommendation → calculate risk/savings → approval/policy → protected change in provider → verify performance/cost → rollback if degraded → record realized savings.

## Integrations / API / data

Cloud providers, Kubernetes, observability, model gateways, DB/storage services, IaC/Git, finance/ERP, ticketing, CMDB, deployment platforms. APIs for costs/resources/recommendations/forecast/budgets/savings.

Data moat: normalized cloud resource/cost graph, workload patterns, verified optimization outcomes and cross-provider mappings; customer configs isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Cloud spend percentage, resources/accounts, seats, verified savings share, enterprise/private, MSP, API/OEM. Distribution through cloud marketplaces, FinOps/SRE communities, MSPs/integrators, observability/IaC partners.

## Security/privacy

Cloud metadata can expose architecture. Least-privilege read-only default, secret refs, protected remediation, no credentials to model, audit, company isolation. Recommendations must respect resilience/security/data residency.

## Failure / edge cases

Unused-looking failover resource, seasonal capacity, reserved commitments, cold start, bursty workload, shared cost tags, egress surprise, storage retrieval fees, performance regression, GPU queue backlog, provider pricing change. Verify before and after; keep rollback and uncertainty.

## Scale/overlap

Single account → enterprise multi-cloud FinOps → autonomous constrained optimization. Overlap #68 AI routing optimizer, #95 ROI, Resource Governor. #043 focuses infrastructure/cloud economics.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** cost/resource telemetry, provider-neutral resource IDs, budgets/quotas, protected infrastructure changes, savings evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Global Resource/Financial Governors need these seams after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** per-company cost centers, provider resource registry, budget/anomaly controls.

# Company 044 — Chargeback & Dispute Recovery Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:044`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:044`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-044-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no dispute filing, financial action or customer communication.

## Business identity

Purpose: organize transaction disputes/chargebacks, assemble evidence, map reason codes and deadlines, recommend prevention actions and measure verified recovery outcomes.

Problem: merchants lose valid revenue because evidence is scattered, deadlines are short and reason-code requirements differ.

Value: complete dispute packets, evidence provenance, readiness checks and root-cause prevention.

## Product tree

Dispute Intake; Reason-Code Normalizer; Deadline Calendar; Transaction/Order Linkage; Customer Communication Evidence; Delivery/Fulfillment Evidence; Usage/Login/Service Evidence; Contract/Policy Evidence; Evidence Packet Builder; Filing Readiness; Response Draft; Outcome/Recovery Tracker; Fraud/Abuse Signals; Prevention Analytics; Merchant/Processor Benchmarking; Alerting; API/OEM; Vertical Packs; Managed Dispute Ops.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: processor/network, dispute ID, reason code/version, amount/currency, transaction/order/customer, deadline/timezone, evidence requirements, source hash/provenance, delivery/usage/refund status, prior contact, terms accepted, fraud signals, packet completeness, outcome, fee/recovery attribution, audit.

Customers: ecommerce, SaaS/digital services, marketplaces, travel/hospitality, subscription businesses, online services, merchants/agencies, enterprise payment teams.

Verticals: physical goods, digital goods, SaaS/subscriptions, marketplaces, bookings/travel, services. Rules/evidence differ by processor/network/jurisdiction.

## Brain / architecture

Brain maps reason codes to evidence requirements, identifies gaps and drafts concise evidence narratives grounded in records. Deterministic deadlines/packet rules and processor schemas own readiness. It cannot fabricate evidence or file disputes without authorization.

Architecture: payment/dispute event ledger, reason-code registry, transaction/order graph, artifact/evidence store, document renderer, rules/checklist, scheduler, fraud analytics, LLM for cited narrative drafting, outcome analytics.

## Agent tree

Dispute Intake Agent, Reason-Code Agent, Evidence Collector, Fulfillment Agent, Usage Evidence Agent, Communication Evidence Agent, Narrative Draft Agent, Readiness QA Agent, Deadline Agent, Fraud/Abuse Agent, Outcome/Reconciliation Agent, Prevention Analyst, Processor Integration Agent.

## Deterministic services

Processor/webhook connectors; transaction/dispute registry; reason-code rules; deadline scheduler; evidence hash/store; packet generator; completeness validator; filing adapter gate; reconciliation; fraud rules; audit.

## Workflow

Dispute event → normalize reason/deadline → link transaction/order/account → collect verified evidence → validate requirements → draft packet → QA → protected filing → monitor processor status → reconcile outcome/fees → attribute recovered amount → feed prevention analytics.

## Integrations / API / data

Payment processors, ecommerce/OMS, shipping/carriers, CRM/support, auth/usage analytics, subscription billing, document storage, fraud systems, accounting. APIs for disputes/evidence/readiness/deadlines/outcomes/prevention.

Data moat: reason/evidence mappings, outcome corpus, processor requirements/version history, fraud/prevention patterns. Customer transaction data isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Disputes/transactions, recovered-value share, subscription, seats, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed ops. Distribution through payment/ecommerce/merchant ecosystems and agencies.

## Security/legal/privacy

Payment/customer evidence sensitive. No card secrets, false evidence or harassment; protect PII; processor terms; filing protected; financial reconciliation exact; audit/retention.

## Failure / edge cases

Reason-code change, duplicate dispute, refund already issued, lost tracking, digital service partial use, customer identity mismatch, deadline timezone, evidence not admissible, processor outage, overturned outcome. Use versioned requirements, evidence confidence and reconciliation.

## Scale/overlap

Merchant tool → enterprise dispute operations. Overlap #57 fraud, #86 payment reconciliation, #92 commerce gateway. #044 focuses merchant dispute evidence/recovery.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** financial event IDs, evidence/provenance, deadline/version, protected filing, reconciliation.  
**BUILD NOW:** generic finance/evidence/protected-action seams after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** processor adapters, financial isolation, document/evidence packaging.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** dispute rules/customer UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** cross-processor benchmark network.

15. Moat Tree: processor reason/evidence corpus and outcomes.
16. Platform Tree: dispute assistant→merchant recovery operations→payment dispute intelligence.
17. Risk Tree: false evidence, PII/payment leakage, missed deadlines, reconciliation errors.
18. Scale Tree: merchant→enterprise→cross-processor platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #57/#86/#92 already cover fraud/reconciliation/commerce.
